sections.title: Basic Concept of Line Graph
sections.content: A Line Graph is a visual representation of data where values are shown as points and connected by straight lines. It is mainly used to show increase or decrease over time such as months, years, or days.

sections.title: Understanding X-axis and Y-axis
sections.content: The horizontal line is called the X-axis. It usually shows time like years or months. The vertical line is called the Y-axis. It shows numbers such as sales, quantity, or amount in rupees.

sections.title: Rupees Based Example
sections.content: Suppose a shop earns 20000 rupees in January, 25000 rupees in February, and 22000 rupees in March. These values are plotted on the graph and connected to show the trend of sales.

sections.title: Identifying Increase and Decrease
sections.content: If the line moves upward, it shows increase. If the line moves downward, it shows decrease. A flat line means there is no change.

sections.title: Finding Highest and Lowest Value
sections.content: The highest point on the graph shows the maximum value. The lowest point shows the minimum value. Always identify these first before solving questions.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: Students often ignore the scale or read the wrong year. Always check the units and scale carefully before answering.

tricks.title: Identify the Trend First
tricks.explanation: Look at the overall direction of the line before solving. It saves time.
tricks.example: If sales move from 10000 to 30000 steadily, the trend is increasing.

tricks.title: Quick Difference Method
tricks.explanation: Subtract the smaller value from the larger value to find change.

tricks.title: Fast Total Calculation
tricks.explanation: Add all values carefully to find total.

tricks.title: Average Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Add all values and divide by the number of periods.

tricks.title: Spot Maximum and Minimum Quickly
tricks.explanation: Check the highest and lowest points first for comparison questions.

tricks.title: Check the Scale Carefully
tricks.explanation: Understand the gap between numbers on the Y-axis.
tricks.example: If scale increases by 5000 each step, count accordingly.

tricks.title: Continuous Growth Trick
tricks.explanation: If each value is higher than the previous one, it shows continuous growth.

tricks.title: Simple Percentage Change
tricks.explanation: Divide the increase by the original value and multiply by 100.
tricks.example: Increase from 20000 to 25000 is 5000. 5000 divided by 20000 times 100 equals 25 percent.
